image_description: A close-up photograph of a brown butterfly, identified as a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), perched vertically on a green blade of grass. The wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is characterized by a warm brown/orange hue and distinct rows of eyespots (ocelli) with white pupils and black rings. The body is slender, dark, and appears hairy. Two clubbed antennae are clearly visible extending from the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two antennae are clearly visible extending from the head; they exhibit the characteristic thickening at the tips (clubs) typical of butterflies.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wings display a base color of brown/orange-brown. There are clear rows of eyespots: two large ones on the forewing and three on the hindwing, matching the diagnostic description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly is perched with wings folded vertically above the body, exposing the underside (ventral) pattern which serves as camouflage.

The thorax appears fuzzy/hairy, and the abdomen is slender, consistent with lepidopteran anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While Ringlets are Nymphalids and possess reduced forelegs, they are tucked against the body and obscured by the angle of the head and thorax in this image. They cannot be visually confirmed or denied.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The division between head, thorax, and abdomen is visible, and the texture suggests a hard exoskeleton.

Verify if the white pupils have any specular highlight or logical placement. Also, check the connection point of the legs to the thorax; ensure they don't appear to melt into the body.
